items.finding: The queue-aware branch is placed after transport semantics and before variable-length runtime planning. It preserves pre-allocated synchronous training, adds facility admission state without transferring optimizer/aggregation authority to the predictor, and states drift, heterogeneity, stale-update and exact-v1 scope boundaries.

The probability-geometry gate follows the beta/update-scale discussion and precedes the system-complexity handoff. Standard DPO remains the baseline for audited in-distribution pairs; the gate only modulates rejected-gradient magnitude, while optimizer commit and preference truth retain their existing owners. Calibration bias, subgroup masking and exact-v1 bounds are explicit.

Virtual execution-resource identity extends the existing fine-grained completion-signal path without replacing fixed-core execution. Readiness controls binding, while completion, visibility and commit remain in the execution plan. Scheduler/state cost, fairness/deadlock risk, fixed-core fallback and hardware/workload evidence limits are explicit.

The branch evolves per-request admission into a cross-window risk state, then hands off to broader time-coupled scheduling. The predictor proposes, the risk accountant constrains admission, and hard deadlines remain external authority. Drift, correlation/fairness failures, conservative EDF/reservation fallback and exact-v1 scope are explicit.

The DP-monitoring branch follows zero-trust aggregation and keeps offline single-release noise as the simpler old path. Event adjacency, temporal specification, barrier placement, noisy release and composition accounting form one state machine; alerting is explicitly only post-processing. Rare-event visibility, budget exhaustion, correlation assumptions, raw-evidence fallback and exact-v1 limits are explicit.

BYOK remains the old credential boundary; the new response-path threat transfers no content-truth authority to signatures. Request/model/digest/freshness identity, consumer verification, provenance-break handling, key/stream/replay costs and direct/retry/human fallback are explicit. The prose correctly marks provider signatures as an unevaluated defense direction in exact-v1.
